subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should managed Gateway and node services get the fixed 8192 MB heap default from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250 now, or should this wait for a first-class tunable heap surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent daemon startup default affects constrained hosts and the existing NODE_OPTIONS security policy, so automation should not choose the rollout policy alone.

options.title: Land fixed default
options.body: Accept the open PR as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the fix until maintainers choose a CLI/config surface with upgrade proof for low-memory hosts.

options.title: Reject daemon heap default
options.body: Close the heap-setting path and focus only on underlying memory growth or state-pruning fixes.

recommendation.title: Land fixed default
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent daemon install/service-env history and was explicitly pulled into the issue timeline.
